- **add CLI-10 (When setup runs again, the CLI shall refresh the…)**: slice 3 builds `spec init`.
  - text: When setup runs again, the CLI shall refresh the files it wrote and leave every other file and setting unchanged.
  - traces_to: SYS-5

  - why: running setup again is how a repository picks up a newer skill or hook, and it must never overwrite the engineer's own settings, such as their other Claude Code hooks.
- **add DR-38 (The skill ships inside the package, and setup installs…)**: slice 3 design.
  - title: The skill ships inside the package, and setup installs it with the launcher's name filled in
  - decided_by: agent
  - elements: AGENT, CLI
  - requirements: AGENT-42, SYS-27, CLI-9
  - recorded: round 11 (slice 3)
  - context: The method is one portable skill (DR-1). It has to reach each repository, and the commands it gives have to work there however the machine installs Python.
  - decision:
    The skill lives in the Python package, so pip installs it. It is SKILL.md plus four reference pages: writing requirements, auditing, onboarding, and the rules page the checker links to.
    - `spec init` copies it to where each harness looks for skills: .claude/skills/syseng for Claude Code, .agents/skills/syseng for Antigravity.
    - The copy has the placeholder {{SPEC}} replaced by the repository's launcher, `.syseng/spec`.
    - The skill names no harness, tool or package manager. Harness-specific parts live in adapters.
  - alternatives: A skill that tells agents to run `spec` from the PATH, which breaks whenever the toolkit lives in a virtual environment the agent's shell hasn't activated. Keeping the skill outside the package, which pip wouldn't install.
  - consequences: The installed copy is committed with the repository, so it can fall behind the toolkit. `spec init --check` reports the difference and `spec init` refreshes it. The rules page moved from docs/ into the skill.
- **add DR-39 (Two launchers, one committed with the repository and one…)**: slice 3 design.
  - title: Two launchers, one committed with the repository and one per machine
  - decided_by: agent
  - elements: CLI
  - requirements: SYS-5, SYS-32, CLI-9
  - recorded: round 11 (slice 3)
  - context: Agents need one command that runs the toolkit in every checkout, including worktrees and teammates' clones, while each machine installs Python its own way. The engineer asked that Nix not be assumed (SYS-32).
  - decision:
    `.syseng/spec` is a short shell script, committed with the repository. It runs this machine's launcher, ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/syseng/launcher.
    - `spec init` writes the machine's launcher to run the Python that ran `spec init`, adding the toolkit's source directory when the toolkit isn't installed as a package.
    - `--launcher CMD` replaces it, for setups such as a Nix shell. An existing launcher that works is otherwise kept.
    - Without a machine launcher, `.syseng/spec` says the toolkit isn't set up and exits with code 127.
  - alternatives: One launcher per repository, ignored by git, which new worktrees and fresh clones don't have. Running `spec` from the PATH, which depends on which environment is active.
  - consequences: `spec init` writes one file outside the repository. A machine with two toolkit installs uses whichever one `spec init --launcher` named last.
- **add DR-40 (Claude Code hooks are one standard-library script, committed with…)**: slice 3 design.
  - title: Claude Code hooks are one standard-library script, committed with the repository
  - decided_by: agent
  - elements: AGENT
  - requirements: AGENT-20, AGENT-12, SYS-27
  - recorded: round 11 (slice 3)
  - context: The spec guard (DR-3), the done gate (DR-4) and chat approvals (DR-6) need hooks. The guard runs before every edit and shell command, so it must be fast, and it should work on a clone where the toolkit isn't installed yet.
  - decision:
    `.syseng/hook` is one Python script that uses only the standard library. `spec init` copies it from the package and registers it in .claude/settings.json for three events: before each tool call, when the agent stops, and when the engineer sends a message.
    - It refuses a tool call by exiting with code 2, giving the reason on standard error.
    - The guard refuses edits to the files the toolkit manages: elements, change records, approvals, retired IDs and generated views. Its refusal names the command to use. toolkit.yaml and hand-written pages such as the glossary stay editable.
    - For shell commands, it refuses plain writes into those files: redirections, tee, rm, mv, cp, and in-place sed or perl.
    - Only the stop and prompt hooks run the toolkit, through the launcher. When the toolkit isn't set up, nothing is blocked, and the engineer sees a notice.
  - alternatives: Hooks that call the toolkit for everything, which costs a Python start-up with PyYAML on every tool call and fails on machines without the toolkit. A Claude Code plugin, which DR-1 ruled out.
  - consequences: A script that opens spec files itself, in python or awk, gets past the guard. The change log and the auditors are the backstop. The hook copy can fall behind the toolkit until `spec init` runs again.
- **add DR-41 (Chat approvals are recorded only when they name items…)**: slice 3 design; it narrows DR-6.
  - title: Chat approvals are recorded only when they name items by ID, and anything else is confirmed first
  - decided_by: agent
  - elements: AGENT
  - requirements: AGENT-21, AGENT-33, AGENT-34, AGENT-43
  - recorded: round 11 (slice 3)
  - context: DR-6 has a hook record chat approvals: a message that starts with "approve" and names the items, or approves everything except some items. A hook can't tell which items "everything" covered in the agent's last message, or which items a described exception refers to (AGENT-43). It also can't see what the engineer was last shown (AGENT-34).
  - decision:
    The prompt hook records an approval only when a message starts with "approve" (or "approved") and its first clause consists of item IDs and ranges.
    - It records the whole message as the engineer's words, marked as given in chat, and tells the agent what it recorded.
    - Any other approval, such as "approve everything except the wording ones", records nothing. The hook tells the agent to show the exact list, leaving out every item an exception could refer to, and to get the engineer's confirmation, in a menu where the harness has one.
    - Pasted text never counts. A message with "lgtm" or "looks good" gets a note that it approves nothing.
  - alternatives: Reading "everything" as every unapproved item in the open change, which can approve items the engineer was never shown. Letting the agent interpret every approval, which DR-6 ruled out.
  - consequences: "Approve everything except …" costs one extra confirmation. An approval covers the items as they are when the engineer sends the message, and the hook asks the agent to say if it changed any of them after showing them. Claude Code also runs this hook for messages from other sessions and from background subagents, so an agent that sent a message starting with "approve" could create an approval. The skill forbids that, and each approval records its words.
- **add DR-42 (The reasoning check's read guard refuses every read or…)**: slice 3 design; it refines DR-7.
  - title: The reasoning check's read guard refuses every read or search that could reach the spec
  - decided_by: agent
  - elements: REASON
  - requirements: REASON-5, REASON-2
  - recorded: round 11 (slice 3)
  - context: DR-7 planned a hook that refuses reads under the spec directory and drops spec hits from search results, and said to fall back to an instruction if that proved fiddly.
  - decision:
    The reasoning-check subagent gets only the read, search and file-listing tools, and its own hook refuses a read inside the spec directory and a search that could return a spec file.
    - A search reaches the spec when it starts inside it, or starts above it with no file filter or with a filter that matches a spec file.
    - Searches filtered to source files, or aimed at source directories, pass.
  - alternatives: Filtering spec hits out of search results afterwards, which Claude Code allows but which means rewriting each tool's output format. The instruction alone.
  - consequences: The guard covers every tool the subagent has. A subagent that searches the whole repository without a filter is refused once, and narrows its search.
- **add DR-43 (Rule links point at the rules page the repository…)**: slice 3 design.
  - title: Rule links point at the rules page the repository has
  - decided_by: agent
  - elements: CHECK
  - requirements: CHECK-16
  - recorded: round 11 (slice 3)
  - context: The checker's findings link to the rule they break (CHECK-16). The rules page was docs/rules.md in the toolkit's repository, so links in every other repository pointed at a file that isn't there.
  - decision: The rules page is part of the skill. A finding links to the toolkit's own copy inside the toolkit's repository, else to the copy `spec init` installed, else to the page inside the installed package.
  - alternatives: A web address, which needs hosting and can disagree with the installed version.
  - consequences: In every repository the toolkit has set up, links are relative paths an editor can open.

- **modify DR-6 (Record chat approvals from the engineer's own message)**: D1 in this round. The engineer said who records an approval doesn't matter; what matters is that the record shows who approved it and how.
  - decision: ~~a Claude Code UserPromptSubmit hook reads the engineer's message. When the message is an explicit approval, the hook records it against the items as they were last shown. The agent never records approvals.~~ → a Claude Code UserPromptSubmit hook reads the engineer's message. When the message is an explicit approval, the hook records it against the items as they were last shown. Approvals the hook can't read, such as a choice in the harness's question menu or an explicit "<ID> LGTM", are recorded by the agent, quoting the engineer's words and naming the channel.
- **modify DR-41 (Chat approvals are recorded only when they name items…)**: the engineer approved SYS-32 by writing "SYS-32 LGTM" on its own line, which the first version of the hook would have reported as approving nothing, contradicting their rule that an unambiguous LGTM in chat counts.
  - decision, before: ~~The prompt hook records an approval only when a message starts with "approve" (or "approved") and its first clause consists of item IDs and ranges. - It records the whole message as the engineer's words, marked as given in chat, and tells the agent what it recorded. - Any other approval, such as "approve everything except the wording ones", records nothing. The hook tells the agent to show the exact list, leaving out every item an exception could refer to, and to get the engineer's confirmation, in a menu where the harness has one. - Pasted text never counts. A message with "lgtm" or "looks good" gets a note that it approves nothing.~~
  - decision, now:
    The prompt hook reads each line of the engineer's message on its own. A line approves when it starts with "approve" (or "approved") and its first clause names only item IDs and ranges, or when it is only item IDs followed by "LGTM", "approved" or "looks good", as in "SYS-32 LGTM".
    - It records the whole message as the engineer's words, marked as given in chat, and tells the agent what it recorded.
    - Any other approval, such as "approve everything except the wording ones", records nothing. The hook tells the agent to show the exact list, leaving out every item an exception could refer to, and to get the engineer's confirmation, in a menu where the harness has one.
    - Quoted lines and pasted text never count, and a capitalized word counts as a system element only when that element exists. A message with "lgtm" or "looks good" and no IDs gets a note that it approves nothing.
- **modify AGENT-V4 (A line that approves items by ID records each…)**: follows the DR-41 change.
  - description: ~~A message whose first clause approves items by ID records each item's approval, with the whole message as the engineer's words, marked as given in chat, and the agent is told what was recorded. Messages that approve "everything", give an exception by description, or mix IDs with other words record nothing, and the agent is told to confirm the exact list. "lgtm" records nothing, pasted text records nothing, and a message naming an unknown ID records nothing.~~ → A line that approves items by ID records each item's approval, with the whole message as the engineer's words, marked as given in chat, and the agent is told what was recorded. Such a line either starts with "approve" or is only IDs followed by "LGTM", and it may be any line of a longer message. Lines that approve "everything", give an exception by description, or mix IDs with other words record nothing, and the agent is told to confirm the exact list. "lgtm" without IDs, quoted lines, pasted text, capitalized words that aren't elements, and unknown IDs record nothing.

It is SKILL.md plus four reference pages: writing requirements, auditing, onboarding, and the rules page the checker links to. - `spec init` copies it to where each harness looks for skills: .claude/skills/syseng for Claude Code, .agents/skills/syseng for Antigravity. - The copy has the placeholder {{SPEC}} replaced by the repository's launcher, `.syseng/spec`. - The skill names no harness, tool or package manager.   - decision, now:
    The skill lives in the Python package, so pip installs it. It is SKILL.md plus four reference pages: writing requirements, auditing, onboarding, and the rules page the checker links to.
    - `spec init` copies it to where each harness looks for skills: .claude/skills/syseng for Claude Code, and .agents/skills/syseng, the cross-tool location that Hermes and Antigravity read. Hermes loads a repository's skills only after `hermes skills trust`.
    - Each copy has the placeholder {{SPEC}} replaced by the repository's launcher, `.syseng/spec`, and {{HARNESS_NOTES}} replaced by what that harness's hooks do, or by a note that none run (AGENT-49).
    - The skill itself names no harness, tool or package manager. Harness-specific parts live in adapters.

## Agent friction

- **Worked around:** Toolkit messages name commands as `spec …` (for example "list them with `spec check --todo`"), but agents in a set-up repository run `.syseng/spec`; an agent following a message literally gets 'command not found' and has to translate. **Proposal:** Have the repository launcher export the name it was run as (SYSENG_PROG=.syseng/spec), and build every command mentioned in messages from it.
